title: Get your GF in the Gym (Girl Fitness Program)
summary: NH presents his first program for women: a 3-day full-body novice routine (Mon/Wed/Fri) built on compounds but weighted toward legs and glutes, with higher reps and minimal upper-body pushing. He explains the exercise choices in terms of female goals, anatomy and injury risk, and advises women to eat enough rather than fear bulk.
claims: Female fitness influencers rarely make serious programs for women because they cater to a male audience
Women respond to training like men physiologically, but their goals differ, so telling them to just train like men is lazy
The women's novice program is 3 full-body days a week (Mon/Wed/Fri), emphasizing legs and glutes with less upper-body work
Women do not have less work capacity than men if trained correctly
Women have relatively higher muscular endurance, so programs for them should favor higher reps and volume
Higher-rep squats help women control knee valgus caused by hip and femur anatomy, making it easier to track knees over toes
Push-ups AMRAP or bench press 4x6-8 (4-8 in the description); little pushing because chest and shoulders respond poorly to hypertrophy in women
Dumbbell curls 4x8-12 as the only biceps movement: women are often gifted in biceps, but most do not want big arms, just toned ones
Decline bench crunches 4x12-15 plus calf raises 4x10-15; calves balance the leg and help prevent knee stabilization problems
Core training will not give a six-pack at 4 sets a week but aids stability, injury prevention and even fat distribution
Women have lower injury rates and recover better from tendon damage, thanks to higher estrogen
Wednesday starts with RDLs 3x8-12, only 3 sets because it is peak posterior-chain fatigue; squats go first on Monday since they are riskier when fatigued
Lat pulldowns 4x10-15 (or cable rows); many women have great upper-back potential
Bent-over lateral raises 4x12-15 instead of standing laterals, since side delts matter little for most women but upper-back shape does
The hip thrust is only bad if it replaces squats and deadlifts; as an added lift it is fine, 4x12-15, always above 10 reps
Triceps pushdowns or chest flies 4x10-15; women will not get bulky arms, it just firms the back of the arm
Friday is lighter on the legs: lunges 4x10-15 or squats 3x6-8, ideally a different squat variation than Monday
Dumbbell overhead press 3x6-10 mainly for injury prevention: women have a higher rotator cuff injury risk and lower bone density, which raises osteoporosis risk
Dumbbell rows 3x8-12 are optional for women who feel it is too much back work
Hyperextensions 4x10-12 serve as active recovery, then standing calf raises 4x12-15
Beginner women must avoid doing too much and burning out mentally; they should modify the program to their liking
Women should eat on a moderate surplus by appetite; the gained fat and muscle will go to legs and glutes, so lift instead of getting butt implants
He plans a separate Casca-from-Berserk program for women who want to be jacked
exercises: higher reps; track knees with toes
glutes, posture; never replaces squats and deadlifts
rotator cuff and shoulder injury prevention
